CHAPTER I 
INTRODUCTION 
 
Background 
The Campus Christian Movement (CCM) is a Christ -centered student organization 
committed to proclaiming the gospel of Jesus Christ, nurturing believers toward spiritual 
maturity, and developing servant leaders who will influence the campus, the church, and 
the community for the glory of God. Recognizing the campus as a strategic mission field, 
CCM exists to provide students with opportunities to encounter Christ, grow in their 
faith, cultivate Christian fellowship, and actively participate in God's mission of making 
disciples. 
 
As a recognized student organization of J.H. Cerilles State College, CCM operates in 
accordance with the policies of the College and under the guidance of its Faculty Adviser, 
while remaining firmly anchored in Biblical principles. Through evangelism, 
discipleship, leadership development, worship, prayer, fellowship, and community 
engagement, the organization seeks to contribute to the holistic development of students 
by nurturing their spiritual, moral, intellectual, emotional, and social well-being. 
 
This Manual of Operations has been developed to provide a comprehensive guide for the 
governance and day -to-day operations of the organization. It establishes standardized 
procedures, operational policies, ministry guidelines, and administrative systems th at 
promote consistency, accountability, and excellence in every aspect of the ministry. More 
than an administrative document, this manual reflects CCM's commitment to serving 
God with integrity, order, and faithfulness, recognizing that effective ministry is 
strengthened by clear direction, responsible stewardship, and intentional discipleship. 
 
 
The provisions contained in this Manual are intended to guide officers, committee heads, 
ministry leaders, members, volunteers, and future generations of student leaders in 
carrying out the mission and vision of the Campus Christian Movement. By documenting 
the organization's operational practices, CCM seeks to preserve its ministry culture, 
ensure continuity of leadership, and sustain a Christ -centered movement that faithfully 
reaches students, builds believers, and equips leaders who will make disciples b eyond 
the campus. 
 
 
Purpose of the Manual 
This Manual of Operations serves as the official operational guide of the Campus 
Christian Movement (CCM). It translates the organization's Constitution and By -Laws 
into practical policies, procedures, and standards that govern the planning, 
implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of all ministry activities.

CCM Manual of Operation 
3 
 
Specifically, the Manual seeks to: 
1. Establish uniform operational procedures for all ministries, programs, and 
organizational activities. 
2. Define the roles, responsibilities, and accountabilities of officers, ministry 
leaders, committee heads, advisers, and members. 
3. Promote Biblical stewardship, servant leadership, transparency, and 
organizational accountability. 
4. Ensure that ministry programs are conducted in an orderly, efficient, safe, and 
Christ-honoring manner. 
5. Preserve institutional memory by documenting operational systems and best 
practices that may be passed on to succeeding generations of leaders. 
6. Support leadership continuity through standardized ministry processes and 
clear administrative guidelines. 
7. Promote compliance with the policies, rules, and regulations of J.H. Cerilles 
State College while fulfilling the organization's spiritual mission. 
8. Encourage excellence in ministry through continuous evaluation, 
improvement, and faithful stewardship of the resources entrusted by God. 
 
Scope and Application 
This Manual of Operations shall apply to all officers, committee heads, ministry leaders, 
Faith Circle leaders, volunteers, members, advisers, and individuals serving under the 
Campus Christian Movement. It governs all official activities, programs, minist ries, 
meetings, trainings, outreaches, leadership development initiatives, financial 
transactions, documentation processes, and organizational operations conducted under 
the authority of CCM. 
 
The Manual shall be observed in conjunction with the Constitution and By -Laws of the 
organization, the policies and regulations of J.H. Cerilles State College, and all applicable 
national laws governing student organizations. In the event of any inconsistency between 
this Manual and the Constitution and By-Laws, the latter shall prevail. 
 
All officers and ministry leaders are expected to become familiar with the provisions of 
this Manual and faithfully implement them in the performance of their responsibilities. 
Members are likewise encouraged to understand the operational principles of the  
organization to promote unity, accountability, and effective participation in the ministry. 
 
 
Guiding Principles 
The operations of the Campus Christian Movement shall be guided by the following 
principles: 
 
1. Christ-Centeredness – Jesus Christ is the foundation, purpose, and ultimate 
authority of every ministry activity.

CCM Manual of Operation 
4 
2. Biblical Faithfulness – All decisions, teachings, programs, and policies shall be 
consistent with the authority of the Holy Scriptures. 
3. Dependence on the Holy Spirit – CCM acknowledges the Holy Spirit as the 
Divine Counselor, Teacher, and Empowerer of believers. Every ministry, decision 
and act of service shall be carried out in prayerful dependence upon His guidance, 
wisdom, conviction, gifting, and power, recognizing that lasting spiritual 
transformation and fruitful ministry are accomplished through His work. 
4. Servant Leadership  – Leadership is exercised through humility, integrity, 
accountability, and a willingness to serve others. 
5. Love and Compassion  – Members shall demonstrate Christlike love, respect, 
and genuine concern toward every individual regardless of background. 
6. Discipleship and Multiplication  – Every believer is encouraged to grow 
spiritually, disciple others, and participate in God's mission of making disciples. 
7. Unity in Diversity – The organization values cooperation, mutual respect, and 
harmonious relationships while recognizing the unique gifts and backgrounds of 
its members. 
8. Integrity and Accountability  – Honesty, transparency, and responsible 
stewardship shall characterize all organizational operations and ministry 
activities. 
9. Partnership – CCM seeks to work collaboratively with the College 
administration, faculty, churches, parents, alumni, and partner organizations in 
advancing its mission. 
10. Continuous Growth  – The organization remains committed to learning, 
innovation, evaluation, and improvement in order to become increasingly 
effective in fulfilling its God-given mission.

CHAPTER II 
ORGANIZATIONAL IDENTITY 
 
 
2.1 Name of the Organization 
 
The organization shall be known as the Campus Christian Movement (CCM), a Christ-
centered student organization established at J.H. Cerilles State College (JHCSC). 
 
CCM exists as a community of students committed to glorifying God by proclaiming the 
gospel of Jesus Christ, making disciples, developing Christ -like leaders, and mobilizing 
believers to become faithful witnesses in the campus, the church, the workplace, and the 
community. 
As a recognized student organization of J.H. Cerilles State College, CCM operates in 
accordance with the policies and regulations of the College while remaining steadfast in 
its commitment to the authority of the Holy Scriptures and the Lordship of Jesus Christ. 
 
 
2.2 Official Logo 
The official logo of the Campus Christian Movement (CCM) serves as the visual identity 
of the organization. It represents the ministry's biblical foundation, spiritual mission, and 
commitment to fulfilling the Great Commission through Christ -centered, Spirit -filled 
discipleship. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Figure 1: CCM Official Logo

Elements and Symbolism 
 
The Outer Circle 
The circular form symbolizes unity, completeness, and the continuous mission of making 
disciples. It reflects the lifelong commitment of CCM members to grow in Christ and 
extend His Kingdom from the campus to the community and beyond. 
 
 
The Blue Ring 
The blue ring represents faithfulness, truth, and spiritual steadfastness. It signifies the 
ministry's unwavering commitment to God's Word and its calling to remain faithful in 
fulfilling the ministry of reconciliation. 
 
The Purple Border 
The purple border symbolizes Christ's kingship, spiritual authority, and the believer's 
identity as part of God's royal priesthood. It reminds every member that Jesus Christ is 
the supreme Head of the ministry. 
 
The Cross 
Positioned at the center of the logo, the cross represents Jesus Christ and His finished 
work of redemption. It declares that Christ is the foundation, message, and focus of every 
ministry, activity, and decision of CCM. 
 
The Dove 
The descending dove symbolizes the Holy Spirit, who guides, empowers, sanctifies, and 
equips believers for holy living and effective ministry. It reflects CCM's commitment to 
being a Spirit-led organization that depends upon God's presence and power. 
 
The Rays of Light 
The rays radiating from the dove represent God's truth, divine guidance, and the 
transforming power of the Gospel. They also signify the illumination of the Holy Spirit 
through His Word and the call for believers to be lights in the campus and the world. 
 
The Reaching Hand 
The hand reaching toward the cross represents every person seeking hope, salvation, and 
reconciliation with God through Jesus Christ. It also symbolizes CCM's mission to 
intentionally reach students with the Gospel and invite them into a growing relationship 
with Christ. 
 
The Scripture Reference (2 Corinthians 5:18) 
The inclusion of 2 Corinthians 5:18 declares the Biblical foundation of the ministry: 
 
"Now all things are of God, who has reconciled us to Himself through Jesus Christ, and has 
given us the ministry of reconciliation."

This verse serves as the official theme verse of CCM and summarizes its God-given 
mission— to proclaim reconciliation through Christ and make faithful disciples who will 
likewise reconcile others to God. 
 
 
2.3 Vision 
A community of Christ-centered students growing in character, leadership, and service, 
who positively influence the campus and beyond. 
 
2.4 Mission 
To reach students with the love of Christ, nurture their spiritual growth, develop servant 
leaders, and equip them to positively influence others. 
 
2.5 Core Values 
The Campus Christian Movement embraces the following core values that guide every 
ministry, relationship, and decision: 
 
Christ-Centeredness 
Jesus Christ is the foundation, focus, and purpose of everything the organization does. 
 
Spirit-Lead 
The Holy Spirit is recognized as the Divine Guide, Counselor and, Empowerer  of 
believers, whose presence and work enable Christlike living, fruitful service, and 
effective disciple-making. 
 
Biblical Authority 
The Holy Scriptures serve as the final authority in matters of faith, doctrine, conduct, 
and ministry. 
 
Prayer Dependence 
Every ministry endeavor is carried out in humble dependence upon God through prayer. 
 
Love and Compassion 
Members seek to demonstrate Christ's love through acceptance, humility, kindness, 
service, and genuine care for others. 
 
Discipleship 
Every believer is called to grow in spiritual maturity and intentionally help others follow 
Christ. 
 
Servant Leadership 
Leadership is expressed through humility, integrity, accountability, and faithful service 
rather than personal recognition.

CCM Manual of Operation

Integrity 
Members are expected to uphold honesty, faithfulness, purity, accountability, and 
consistency between belief and practice. 
 
Unity 
The organization values teamwork, mutual respect, and harmonious relationships while 
celebrating the diversity of gifts within the Body of Christ. 
 
Mission 
Every member is called to participate actively in God's mission by proclaiming the Gospel 
and making disciples wherever God has placed them. 
 
 
2.5 Statement of Faith  
The Campus Christian Movement affirms the essential doctrines of the Christian faith as 
revealed in the Holy Scriptures. 
 
The organization believes: 
1. That the Holy Bible is the inspired, infallible, and authoritative Word of God. 
2. That there is one true God, eternally existing in three Persons: the Father, the 
Son, and the Holy Spirit. 
3. That Jesus Christ is fully God and fully man, who lived a sinless life, died for 
the sins of humanity, rose bodily from the dead, ascended into heaven, and will 
return again. 
4. That salvation is by the grace of God alone through faith alone in Jesus Christ 
alone, and not by human works. 
5. That every person is separated from God because of sin and needs the saving 
work of Jesus Christ. 
6. That the Holy Spirit indwells every believer, empowering them to live a holy 
life and participate in God's mission. 
7. That the Church is the body of Christ, composed of all believers, called to 
worship God, make disciples, and proclaim the Gospel. 
8. That every believer is commissioned by Jesus Christ to make disciples of all 
nations. 
9. That Jesus Christ will personally return to establish His eternal kingdom and 
that all people will face eternal judgment. 
 
 
2.6 Ministry Philosophy 
The Campus Christian Movement believes that the college campus is one of the most 
strategic mission fields for advancing the Kingdom of God. Students are not merely 
future leaders; they are present-day ambassadors of Christ who can influence their peers, 
families, churches, workplaces, and communities.

CCM Manual of Operation 
9 
 
Accordingly, CCM adopts a ministry philosophy that emphasizes evangelism, 
intentional discipleship, servant leadership, and multiplication. The organization seeks 
not only to gather students for Christian fellowship but to equip them to become mature 
disciples who faithfully make disciples of others. 
 
This philosophy is expressed through the organization's ministry pathway — from 
reaching students with the Gospel, receiving them into Christian fellowship, rooting 
them in Biblical truth, reproducing disciples through leadership development, and 
releasing them to serve faithfully wherever God calls them. Every ministry, program, and 
organizational activity shall support this mission of developing lifelong followers of Jesus 
Christ who impact society for the glory of God. 
 
2.7 Theme Verse 
"Now all things are of God, who has reconciled us to Himself through Jesus Christ, and 
has given us the ministry of reconciliation." 
—  2 Corinthians 5:18 (NKJV) 
 
This verse embodies the heart of the Campus Christian Movement. Through Jesus Christ, 
God has reconciled us to Himself and entrusted us with the ministry of reconciliation. As 
a Christ -centered campus ministry, CCM is committed to proclaiming the Gospel, 
making disciples, nurturing spiritual growth, developing servant leaders, and equipping 
students to become ambassadors of Christ who bring the message of reconciliation to the 
campus, the community, and beyond.

CHAPTER III 
MINISTRY FRAMEWORK 
 
 
3.1 Ministry Philosophy 
The Campus Christian Movement (CCM) adopts a ministry framework that is rooted in 
the Great Commission of Jesus Christ (Matthew 28:19–20). The organization believes that 
genuine transformation begins with the proclamation of the Gospel, continues through 
intentional discipleship, develops into Christ -like leadership, and ultimately results in 
believers who faithfully make disciples of others. 
 
CCM recognizes the college campus as a strategic mission field where students encounter 
diverse ideas, cultures, and life -shaping experiences. During these formative years, 
students are especially receptive to the Gospel and capable of becoming influential  
witnesses for Christ. Accordingly, the ministry is intentionally designed not merely to 
gather students for fellowship but to lead them toward spiritual maturity and prepare 
them to impact society for the glory of God. 
 
The ministry framework follows a progressive pathway in which students are reached 
with the Gospel, welcomed into Christian fellowship, grounded in Biblical truth, 
equipped for leadership, and released to serve in their families, churches, professions, 
and communities. Every ministry, activity, program, and leadership initiative shall 
contribute to this lifelong process of disciple-making. 
 
3.2 The CCM 5R Ministry Cycle 
To implement its ministry framework, the Campus Christian Movement adopts the 5R 
Ministry Cycle as its operational disciple-making process. 
 
The 5R Ministry Cycle provides a systematic pathway that guides students from their 
first encounter with the Gospel to becoming mature disciples who actively disciple 
others. Rather than functioning as isolated activities, the five stages form a continuous  
cycle of spiritual multiplication. 
 
The five stages are: 
 
Reach – Proclaim Christ to every student through intentional evangelism, personal 
relationships, prayer, campus engagement, and Gospel-centered activities. 
 
Receive – Welcome students who respond to Christ by providing loving acceptance, 
initial follow-up, encouragement, and opportunities to begin their journey of faith within 
the Christian community.

CCM Manual of Operation 
11 
Root – Establish believers upon the foundation of God's Word through Biblical teaching, 
prayer, Christian fellowship, Faith Circles, and foundational discipleship such as the 
SPARK curriculum. 
 
Reproduce – Equip growing disciples to become disciple -makers and servant leaders 
through leadership training, ministry involvement, mentoring, and intentional 
multiplication. 
 
Release – Commission mature believers to faithfully serve Christ in the campus, local 
churches, workplaces, communities, and wherever God calls them, while continuing the 
ministry of making disciples. 
 
Because disciple-making is lifelong, individuals who are released into ministry continue 
participating in the cycle by reaching others with the Gospel and helping them become 
faithful followers of Jesus Christ.

3.2 The Campus to Community Framework 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The Campus to Community Framework  serves as the overarching ministry strategy of 
the Campus Christian Movement. It illustrates the organization's commitment to making 
disciples whose influence extends beyond the college campus into every sphere of 
society. 
 
The framework recognizes that the campus is not the final destination of ministry but the 
starting point of a lifelong mission. Students who encounter Christ during their college 
years are discipled, equipped, and empowered to become faithful followers of Jesus who 
influence their homes, churches, workplaces, professions, communities, and future 
generations. 
 
This framework affirms that every believer is called not only to grow spiritually but also 
to participate actively in God's mission by making disciples wherever He leads. 
Consequently, all CCM programs, leadership structures, discipleship processes, and 
ministry activities are intentionally aligned toward developing Christ-centered graduates 
who continue advancing God's Kingdom beyond the campus.

3.4 Operational Ministries 
The Campus Christian Movement carries out its ministry through interconnected 
programs that collectively support the disciple-making process. 
 
These ministries include, but are not limited to: 
 
Campus Evangelism  
Gospel proclamation through personal evangelism, campus outreaches, prayer 
initiatives, classroom connections (when permitted), and relationship-building activities. 
 
LACS (Lessons for Aspiring Christ's Students)  
LACS is the foundational discipleship program of CCM designed for new believers, 
seekers, and students who desire to grow in their faith. The program utilizes the SPARK 
curriculum to establish participants in the essential truths of the Christian faith, cultivate 
foundational spiritual disciplines, and prepare them for continued growth through 
discipleship. 
 
Christ's Students Institute (CSI) 
Christ's Students Institute (CSI) is the evangelism training program of CCM. It equips 
members with a Biblical understanding of the Gospel and develops the knowledge, skills, 
and confidence needed to share their faith effectively. Participants receive prac tical 
training in personal evangelism, apologetics, Gospel presentation, campus outreach, 
follow-up, and leading others to Christ, preparing them to become faithful witnesses 
within the campus and beyond. 
 
Inner Circle Academy (ICA) 
Inner Circle Academy (ICA) is the discipleship and leadership formation program of 
CCM. Building upon the evangelistic foundation established through CSI, ICA equips 
members to intentionally disciple others, facilitate Faith Circles, mentor younger 
believers, and lead ministries with biblical conviction, spiritual maturity, and servant 
leadership. The program emphasizes multiplication by preparing disciple -makers who 
can nurture others toward spiritual maturity. 
 
 
Leadership Support System (LSS) 
The Leadership Support System (LSS) is the advanced leadership development program 
of CCM, providing specialized formation according to the participant's stage of ministry. 
 
For student leaders , LSS develops organizational leadership, ministry administration, 
team building, strategic planning, event management, mentoring, and collaborative 
leadership to strengthen the ministry within the College and prepare future 
organizational leaders.

CCM Manual of Operation 
14 
For CCM alumni , LSS provides continuing leadership development focused on 
expanding God's Kingdom beyond the campus. Alumni are equipped to establish and 
lead outreach ministries, mentor younger leaders, strengthen partnerships with local 
churches, support the ongoing m inistries of CCM, and contribute to the long -term 
sustainability and multiplication of the Campus Christian Movement. 
 
Faith Circles  
Small-group discipleship communities that provide Biblical instruction, accountability, 
fellowship, pastoral care, and spiritual encouragement. 
 
BLAST (Bible Learning and Spiritual Training)  
A regular gathering focused on Biblical teaching, worship, prayer, leadership 
development, and spiritual growth. 
 
Gather & Grow  
A fellowship -centered ministry that promotes Christian community, encouragement, 
mutual care, and relationship-building among members. 
 
 
Community Outreach and Missions  
Ministry activities that extend Christ's love beyond the campus through evangelism, 
compassion ministries, partnerships with churches, and community engagement. 
 
Each ministry shall function according to its respective objectives, curriculum, 
operational guidelines, and evaluation procedures as provided in subsequent chapters of 
this Manual. 
 
 
3.5 Ministry Integration 
Every ministry, committee, event, and organizational activity of the Campus Christian 
Movement shall intentionally support at least one stage of the 5R Ministry Cycle. 
 
Programs shall not exist as independent activities but shall function together as an 
integrated disciple -making system that advances the mission and vision of the 
organization. Officers, ministry leaders, and volunteers are expected to plan, implement, 
and evaluate all ministry initiatives according to their contribution to evangelism, 
discipleship, leadership development, and multiplication. 
 
The effectiveness of the ministry shall therefore be measured not merely by attendance 
at events, but by evidence of transformed lives, growing disciples, emerging servant 
leaders, healthy Christian communities, and the multiplication of faithful followers  of 
Jesus Christ who continue His mission beyond the campus.

CHAPTER IV 
ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE AND GOVERNANCE 
 
 
4.1 Organizational Governance 
The Campus Christian Movement (CCM) shall operate under a system of shared 
leadership characterized by servant leadership, accountability, mutual respect, and 
Biblical stewardship. The organization recognizes Jesus Christ as its supreme Head, from 
whom all authority and direction ultimately proceed. 
 
The governance of CCM shall be exercised through the Faculty Adviser, the Executive 
Council, committee heads, ministry leaders, and the general membership. Leadership 
shall function collaboratively, recognizing that every officer and member serves as a 
steward entrusted with advancing the mission of the organization. 
 
All leaders are expected to exercise their responsibilities in accordance with the Holy 
Scriptures, the Constitution and By -Laws of the Campus Christian Movement, this 
Manual of Operations, and the policies of J.H. Cerilles State College. Leadership positions 
are opportunities for service rather than privilege, requiring humility, integrity, 
faithfulness, accountability, and a commitment to the spiritual welfare of the members. 
 
Organizational decisions shall be guided by prayer, Biblical wisdom, collective 
discernment, and the best interests of the ministry for the glory of God. 
 
 
4.2 Organizational Structure 
The organizational structure of the Campus Christian Movement is designed to promote 
effective leadership, clear accountability, efficient communication, and coordinated

4.4 Faculty Adviser 
The Faculty Adviser serves as the primary mentor, spiritual guide, and institutional 
representative of the Campus Christian Movement. The Adviser provides guidance, 
oversight, and encouragement to ensure that the organization remains faithful to its 
Vision, Mission, Core Values, Constitution and By-Laws, and the policies of J.H. Cerilles 
State College. 
 
In partnership with the student leaders, the Faculty Adviser fosters a Christ-centered and 
Spirit-led ministry by encouraging dependence on the Holy Spirit through prayer, 
biblical discernment, and faithful obedience to God's Word. While empowering students 
to exercise servant leadership and take ownership of the ministry, the Adviser provides 
wisdom, accountability, continuity, and pastoral support in fulfilling the mission of 
making disciples. 
 
The Faculty Adviser shall: 
1. Provide spiritual guidance and biblical counsel to officers and members. 
2. Encourage leaders and members to seek the guidance and empowering work of 
the Holy Spirit in prayer, decision-making, ministry, and Christian living.

3. Ensure that organizational activities are consistent with the Vision, Mission, 
Core Values, Constitution and By -Laws, this Manual of Operations, and College 
policies. 
4. Advise and mentor the Executive Council in planning, leadership development, 
and ministry implementation. 
5. Promote servant leadership, unity, and spiritual maturity among members. 
6. Review and endorse organizational plans, reports, and official documents as 
required. 
7. Coordinate with College officials, partner churches, alumni, and other 
stakeholders when appropriate. 
8. Support leadership succession by mentoring emerging student leaders and 
preserving the continuity of the ministry. 
9. Encourage accountability, responsible stewardship, and ethical conduct in all 
organizational affairs. 
10. Provide guidance during significant organizational concerns while 
empowering student leaders to prayerfully discern and fulfill their God -given 
responsibilities. 
 
4.5 Executive Council 
The Executive Council is the highest student governing body of the Campus Christian 
Movement and is responsible for the overall leadership, coordination, and administration 
of the organization. 
 
The Executive Council shall: 
1. Formulate ministry plans aligned with the Vision, Mission, and Ministry 
Framework of CCM. 
2. Coordinate all organizational programs and activities. 
3. Supervise committees, ministry teams, and Faith Circles. 
4. Ensure compliance with this Manual of Operations and the Constitution and 
By-Laws. 
5. Manage organizational resources responsibly. 
6. Review ministry reports and evaluate organizational performance. 
7. Recommend policy improvements and operational enhancements. 
8. Promote leadership development and succession planning. 
9. Strengthen partnerships with the College, churches, alumni, and partner 
organizations. 
 
The Executive Council shall conduct its responsibilities collectively, recognizing that 
leadership decisions are strengthened through prayer, collaboration, and mutual 
accountability. 
 
4.6 Committees and Ministry Teams 
To facilitate efficient ministry operations, the Executive Council may establish standing 
or special committees and ministry teams as necessary.

CCM Manual of Operation 
19 
 
 
 
Standing committees may include, but are not limited to: 
• Spiritual Formation 
• Evangelism and Outreach 
• Discipleship 
• Worship and Music 
• Prayer Ministry 
• Training and Leadership Development 
• Communications and Multimedia 
• Documentation 
• Finance 
• Logistics and Events 
• Membership and Fellowship 
 
The Executive Council may create, merge, reorganize, or dissolve committees based on 
the evolving needs of the organization, provided such actions remain consistent with the 
Constitution and By-Laws. 
 
Each committee shall prepare annual ministry plans, implement assigned 
responsibilities, submit accomplishment reports, and participate in organizational 
evaluation processes. 
 
4.7 Decision-Making Process 
The Campus Christian Movement values collaborative and prayerful decision -making. 
Significant organizational decisions shall be reached through consultation, careful 
deliberation, and collective discernment while seeking the guidance of the Holy Spirit 
through prayer and the wisdom of God's Word. 
 
Whenever practical, decisions shall be made by consensus. When consensus cannot be 
achieved, matters may be resolved through a majority vote of the Executive Council, 
unless otherwise provided in the Constitution and By-Laws. 
 
Major organizational matters, including annual plans, budgets, major events, 
amendments to operational policies, and strategic ministry initiatives, shall be presented 
to the Faculty Adviser for guidance and, where required, institutional approval. 
 
All official decisions shall be documented in the minutes of meetings and communicated 
promptly to the appropriate officers, committees, and members. 
 
4.8 Meetings 
Regular meetings are essential for prayer, planning, coordination, accountability, and 
evaluation.

CCM Manual of Operation 
20 
The organization shall conduct the following meetings: 
 
Executive Council Meetings  – Held regularly to discuss ministry plans, organizational 
concerns, financial matters, and upcoming activities. 
 
Committee Meetings  – Conducted as needed to coordinate ministry -specific 
responsibilities. 
 
Leadership Meetings  – Gatherings of officers, committee heads, ministry leaders, and 
Faith Circle Leaders for strategic planning, leadership development, and organizational 
alignment. 
 
General Assembly  – Convened at least once every semester to communicate ministry 
updates, celebrate accomplishments, strengthen fellowship, and present organizational 
directions. 
 
Meetings shall be conducted in an orderly manner, beginning and ending with prayer 
whenever possible. Minutes shall be prepared by the Secretary and maintained as part of 
the organization's permanent records. 
 
 
4.9 Leadership Succession and Continuity 
The Campus Christian Movement recognizes that effective leadership is sustained 
through intentional discipleship, mentoring, and the faithful development of future 
leaders. Leadership succession is therefore regarded as a continuous ministry 
responsibility rather than a periodic organizational activity. 
 
CCM is committed to preparing succeeding generations of leaders who embody Christ -
like character, spiritual maturity, servant leadership, and a deep commitment to the 
mission of making disciples. Every officer, ministry leader, and Faith Circle Leader shares 
the responsibility of identifying, mentoring, and equipping potential leaders who 
demonstrate faithfulness, teachability, integrity, and a willingness to serve. 
 
Leadership development follows the organization's established discipleship pathway, 
which provides progressive opportunities for spiritual growth, ministry involvement, 
leadership training, and increasing responsibility. While individual journeys may vary 
according to spiritual maturity and ministry readiness, the general pathway is as follows:

CCM Manual of Operation 
21 
 
 
 
Advancement within this pathway shall not be based solely on seniority, popularity, or 
academic standing, but primarily on demonstrated Christian character, spiritual growth, 
ministry faithfulness, leadership potential, and readiness to assume greater 
responsibility. Leaders shall be evaluated through prayerful discernment, mentorship, 
observation, and appropriate consultation with the Executive Council and the Faculty 
Adviser. 
 
To ensure continuity of ministry, outgoing officers and ministry leaders shall 
intentionally prepare their successors through mentoring, skills transfer, documentation 
of responsibilities, and orientation on organizational policies and ministry practices. 
Transition meetings shall be conducted to facilitate the orderly transfer of leadership 
responsibilities, records, financial documents, ministry resources, and ongoing projects. 
 
Through intentional leadership succession, the Campus Christian Movement seeks to 
preserve its mission, values, ministry culture, and organizational integrity while 
continually raising Christ-centered leaders who will faithfully advance God's Kingdom 
from the campus to the community and beyond.

CHAPTER V 
MEMBERSHIP 
 
 
5.1 Membership Policy 
The Campus Christian Movement (CCM) welcomes all bona fide students of J.H. Cerilles 
State College who desire to learn about Jesus Christ, grow in their Christian faith, and 
participate in the life and ministry of the organization. Membership is open regardless of 
academic program, year level, gender, ethnicity, or socio -economic backgrou nd, 
provided that the individual agrees to respect the Vision, Mission, Core Values, 
Constitution and By-Laws, and the policies of the organization. 
 
CCM recognizes that students come from different spiritual backgrounds and stages of 
faith. Accordingly, the organization seeks to provide an environment where every 
student is loved, respected, encouraged, and given opportunities to encounter Christ, 
grow spiritually, and discover God's purpose for their lives. 
Membership in CCM is both a privilege and a responsibility. Members are encouraged to 
pursue spiritual maturity, demonstrate Christ -like character, actively participate in 
ministry, and contribute to the fulfillment of the organization's mission of making 
disciples. 
 
5.2 Categories of membership 
To provide appropriate opportunities for participation and leadership, CCM recognizes 
the following categories of membership: 
 
A. Visitor 
A Visitor is any student who attends a CCM activity, fellowship, Bible study, outreach, 
or special event without formally joining the organization. Visitors are warmly welcomed 
and encouraged to participate in activities appropriate to their level of involvement. 
 
C. Regular Members 
Regular Members are bona fide students of J.H. Cerilles  State College who have 
expressed their commitment to the Vision, Mission, Core Values, and objectives of the 
Campus Christian Movement. To qualify as a Regular Member, a student must be 
officially enrolled in the College, accomplish and submit the prescri bed CCM 
Membership Form, demonstrate a willingness to uphold the Constitution and By -Laws 
and this Manual of Operations, and actively participate in the ministries, discipleship 
programs, and activities of the organization. Regular Members are entitled to the rights, 
privileges, and responsibilities provided under this Manual and the Constitution and By-
Laws of the Campus Christian Movement.

CCM Manual of Operation 
23 
C. Active Member 
An Active Member is a Regular Member who consistently participates in worship 
gatherings, discipleship activities, Faith Circles, ministry opportunities, and 
organizational events. Active Members may be entrusted with ministry responsibilities 
and may qualify for leadership development programs. 
 
D. Ministry Leader 
A Ministry Leader is an Active Member who has completed the necessary discipleship 
and leadership preparation and has been entrusted with specific ministry responsibilities, 
such as leading a Faith Circle, serving as a committee head, mentoring members, or  
coordinating ministry programs. 
 
E. Alumni Member 
An Alumni  Member is a former student who was previously active in CCM and 
continues to support the organization through prayer, mentoring, resource sharing, or 
participation in alumni activities. Alumni serve as ministry partners but shall not 
participate in student governance unless otherwise authorized. 
 
 
5.3 Admission to Membership 
Students who desire to become members of CCM shall be welcomed through a process 
that emphasizes relationship, discipleship, and spiritual growth rather than mere 
registration. 
 
 
The membership process generally includes: 
1. Participation in a CCM gathering, outreach, fellowship, or ministry activity. 
2. Introduction to the Vision, Mission, and ministry of CCM. 
3. Completion of the official Membership Information Form, where applicable. 
4. Assignment to a Faith Circle or ministry mentor whenever practicable. 
5. Encouragement to participate in the LACS foundational discipleship program. 
6. Inclusion in appropriate communication channels and ministry activities for 
God’s glory. 
 
No student shall be denied participation on the basis of race, ethnicity, disability, or 
economic status. Membership shall always be extended with Christian love, respect, and 
hospitality, while maintaining compliance with the policies of J.H. Cerilles State College. 
 
5.4 Rights and Privileges of Members 
Every member of the Campus Christian Movement shall enjoy the following rights and 
privileges: 
1. To participate in the worship services, fellowships, Bible studies, discipleship 
programs, leadership trainings, and ministry activities of the organization.

CCM Manual of Operation

2. To receive spiritual care, encouragement, mentoring, and discipleship 
opportunities. 
3. To express ideas, suggestions, and concerns in an orderly and respectful 
manner. 
4. To vote and be elected to positions in accordance with the Constitution and By-
Laws, where applicable. 
5. To receive fair and respectful treatment regardless of personal background. 
6. To access organizational information that is appropriate for members. 
7. To participate in leadership development opportunities based on readiness and 
ministry qualifications. 
 
5.5 Responsibilities of Members 
Every member shares in the responsibility of advancing the mission of the Campus 
Christian Movement. Members are therefore expected to: 
 
1. Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus Christ through prayer, worship, Bible 
study, and obedience to God's Word. 
2. Live a life that reflects Christian character and integrity. 
3. Support the Vision, Mission, Core Values, and ministry objectives of CCM. 
4. Participate faithfully in worship gatherings, Faith Circles, discipleship 
programs, and ministry activities. 
5. Demonstrate love, respect, humility, and unity toward fellow members and the 
College community. 
6. Use their God-given gifts, abilities, and resources in serving the ministry. 
7. Respect the authority of organizational leaders and comply with approved 
organizational policies. 
8. Represent Christ and CCM honorably both on and off campus, including in 
digital and social media spaces. 
9. Help create a welcoming environment where every student has the opportunity 
to know Christ and grow in faith. 
 
5.6 Membership Growth Pathway 
CCM encourages every member to grow intentionally through a progressive pathway of 
spiritual formation and ministry involvement. While individual journeys may differ, 
members are encouraged to advance through the following stages  (refer to Figure 6 
below) 
 
This pathway reflects the organization's commitment to developing mature followers of 
Jesus Christ who faithfully disciple others and participate in God's mission beyond the 
campus. 
 
Progress along the pathway shall be encouraged through mentoring, discipleship, 
leadership development, ministry opportunities, and regular spiritual guidance.

CCM Manual of Operation

5.7 Membership Discipline and Restoration 
The Campus Christian Movement is committed to maintaining a Christ -centered 
community characterized by love, holiness, accountability, and grace. When concerns 
arise regarding a member's conduct, every effort shall be made to restore the individual 
through Biblical counsel, prayer, encouragement, and appropriate mentoring. 
 
Members are expected to uphold the ethical standards of the organization and conduct 
themselves in a manner that honors Christ, respects others, and preserves the integrity of 
CCM. Situations involving repeated misconduct, behavior that brings disrepute to  the 
organization, or persistent disregard of organizational policies may be addressed 
through pastoral conversations, guidance from ministry leaders, and, when necessary, 
review by the Executive Council in consultation with the Faculty Adviser. 
 
Any corrective action shall be undertaken with fairness, confidentiality, compassion, and 
the primary objective of spiritual restoration rather than punishment. Members who 
demonstrate repentance, accountability, and a renewed commitment to Christian livin g 
shall be welcomed and supported in their restoration to active participation in the life 
and ministry of the organization.

CHAPTER VI 
MINISTRY PROGRAMS AND OPERATIONS 
 
 
 
6.1 General Policy 
The Campus Christian Movement (CCM) fulfills its mission through ministry programs 
that intentionally lead students from their first encounter with Jesus Christ toward 
spiritual maturity, servant leadership, and lifelong disciple -making. Every ministry, 
activity, and event shall support the organization's Vision, Mission, Core Values, Campus 
to Community Framework, and the 5R Ministry Cycle. 
 
All ministry programs shall be planned and implemented prayerfully, guided by the 
Holy Scriptures, and conducted in a manner that reflects excellence, integrity, 
accountability, and love. Programs shall be evaluated regularly to ensure that they 
remain Bib lically faithful, relevant to the needs of students, and effective in 
accomplishing the disciple-making mission of CCM. 
 
Every ministry shall encourage active participation, foster genuine Christian fellowship, 
promote spiritual growth, and provide opportunities for members to discover and use 
their God-given gifts in service to God and others. 
 
6.2 The 5R Ministry Cycle 
The Campus Christian Movement organizes all ministry programs according to the 5R 
Ministry Cycle. Each ministry contributes to one or more stages of the disciple -making 
process (refer to Figure 2). 
 
6.3 Reach Ministries 
The Reach Ministries are designed to proclaim the Gospel and intentionally connect with 
students who have not yet encountered Jesus Christ or who are seeking spiritual 
direction. 
 
Reach Ministries may include: 
• Personal Evangelism 
• Friendship Evangelism 
• Campus Prayer Walks 
• Classroom and Campus Engagement (subject to College policies) 
• Evangelistic Fellowships 
• Welcome Booths during enrollment and opening of classes 
• FIRST (Faith-Inspired Return of Students Together) 
• Testimony Nights 
• Gospel Conversations 
• Community Evangelism

CCM Manual of Operation 
29 
The objectives of Reach Ministries are to: 
1. Build meaningful relationships with students. 
2. Share the Gospel in a clear and Biblical manner. 
3. Pray intentionally for students and the campus. 
4. Invite students into Christian fellowship. 
5. Connect interested students with Faith Circles and follow-up ministries. 
Every member is encouraged to participate actively in evangelistic efforts as part of 
fulfilling the Great Commission. 
 
6.4 Receive Ministries 
The Receive Ministries provide intentional care, encouragement, and initial discipleship 
for students who begin participating in CCM. 
 
These ministries include: 
• Welcome and Hospitality 
• New Members Orientation 
• Follow-up Ministry 
• Prayer Partners 
• Fellowship Activities 
• Faith Circle Placement 
 
The Receive Ministries seek to ensure that every newcomer experiences genuine 
Christian love, meaningful relationships, and opportunities for continued spiritual 
growth. 
 
No student should feel unnoticed or disconnected after attending a CCM activity. 
Officers, Faith Circle Leaders, and members share the responsibility of welcoming, 
encouraging, and walking alongside new participants. 
 
6.5 Root Ministries 
Root Ministries establish believers upon the truth of God's Word and cultivate habits 
essential to lifelong spiritual growth. 
 
The primary Root Ministries include: 
 
SPARK 
The foundational discipleship curriculum that introduces students to the essential 
teachings of the Christian faith and establishes Biblical foundations for Christian living. 
 
Faith Circles 
Small-group communities that provide Bible study, prayer, accountability, pastoral care, 
fellowship, and opportunities for spiritual growth.

CCM Manual of Operation 
30 
BLAST 
The organization's regular corporate gathering focused on worship, Biblical teaching, 
prayer, discipleship, leadership development, and encouragement. 
 
Gather & Grow 
A fellowship -centered ministry that strengthens relationships, promotes Christian 
community, and encourages members through meaningful interaction and shared 
experiences. 
 
TURF (The Upper Room Fellowship) 
Regular corporate prayer initiatives that cultivate dependence upon God and intercede 
for students, the College, churches, and the community. 
 
Together, these ministries help believers become spiritually grounded, Biblically 
equipped, and actively connected to the Body of Christ. 
 
6.6 Reproduce Ministries 
The Reproduce Ministries equip growing disciples to become effective disciple -makers 
and servant leaders. 
 
These ministries include: 
 
Christ's Students Institute (CSI) 
Advanced discipleship and ministry training designed to deepen Biblical understanding, 
strengthen ministry competencies, and prepare members for leadership responsibilities. 
 
Ministry Teams 
Practical ministry assignments that allow members to discover and develop their 
spiritual gifts while serving alongside experienced leaders. 
 
Mentoring 
Intentional one -on-one or small -group relationships where mature believers guide 
younger disciples in spiritual growth, ministry involvement, and Christian character. 
 
Leadership Development 
Training programs, workshops, retreats, and ministry experiences that prepare members 
for future leadership within CCM and beyond. 
 
These ministries emphasize multiplication by equipping disciples to disciple others 
faithfully. 
 
6.7 Release Ministries 
Release Ministries prepare mature disciples to continue God's mission beyond the 
campus.

CCM Manual of Operation 
31 
 
These ministries include: 
 
Inner Circle Academy (ICA) 
The highest level of leadership formation within CCM, preparing committed leaders for 
long-term ministry, servant leadership, mentoring, and Kingdom influence. 
 
Commissioning Services 
Special gatherings where graduating students, ministry leaders, and missionaries are 
prayed over and commissioned for continued service in their future fields of influence. 
 
Community Outreach 
Evangelistic, compassion, educational, and service initiatives that demonstrate Christ's 
love within surrounding communities. 
 
Church Partnership 
Encouraging members to become actively involved in Bible -believing, Spirit -led local 
churches for continued spiritual growth, accountability, and service. 
 
LSS (Leadership Support System) Alumni 
Maintaining relationships with graduates who continue supporting CCM through 
mentoring, prayer, resource sharing, and collaborative ministry. 
 
Release Ministries affirm that graduation marks not the end of discipleship but the 
beginning of a broader mission field. 
 
6.8 Ministry Planning and Evaluation 
Each ministry shall prepare an annual ministry plan that supports the Vision, Mission, 
and strategic objectives of the Campus Christian Movement. Ministry plans should 
identify goals, target participants, key activities, responsible leaders, required resources, 
implementation timelines, and expected outcomes. 
 
At the conclusion of every major activity and at the end of each semester, ministry leaders 
shall conduct an evaluation to assess the effectiveness of their programs. Evaluations 
shall consider both quantitative indicators, such as attendance and participa tion, and 
qualitative indicators, including spiritual growth, discipleship progress, leadership 
development, and ministry impact. 
 
Findings from these evaluations shall be documented and submitted to the Executive 
Council. The results shall guide future planning, strengthen ministry effectiveness, and 
promote continuous improvement in fulfilling the mission of CCM.

CHAPTER VII 
MINISTRY OPERATIONS 
 
 
7.1 General Operational Policy 
All ministry activities of the Campus Christian Movement (CCM) shall be conducted in 
an orderly, Christ-centered, and purposeful manner consistent with the Vision, Mission, 
Core Values, Campus to Community Framework, and the 5R Ministry Cycle. 
 
Every activity shall be planned prayerfully, implemented with excellence, and evaluated 
for continuous improvement. Officers, ministry leaders, and volunteers shall work 
collaboratively to create an environment that promotes worship, discipleship, fellowship, 
evangelism, leadership development, and spiritual growth. 
 
All official activities shall comply with the policies of J.H. Cerilles State College and shall 
uphold the highest standards of Christian integrity, stewardship, safety, and 
accountability. 
 
7.2 Weekly Ministry Schedule 
To provide consistency in ministry, CCM shall maintain a regular schedule of 
discipleship and fellowship activities. The Executive Council may adjust the schedule 
when necessary, subject to the approval of the Faculty Adviser. 
 
The regular weekly ministries include: 
• BLAST (Bible Learning and Spiritual Training)  – Weekly corporate worship, 
Biblical teaching, prayer, and discipleship. 
• Gather & Grow  – Weekly fellowship designed to strengthen relationships, 
encourage members, and build Christian community. 
• Faith Circles – Small-group gatherings for Bible study, accountability, prayer, 
and pastoral care. 
• TURF (The Upper Room Fellowship)  – Scheduled prayer gatherings for the 
campus, members, churches, and ministry concerns. 
• Leadership Meetings  – Regular meetings of officers, committee heads, and 
ministry leaders for planning, coordination, and evaluation. 
 
The official ministry calendar shall be prepared every semester and approved by the 
Executive Council in consultation with the Faculty Adviser.

BLAST serves as CCM's primary weekly corporate gathering for worship, Biblical 
instruction, discipleship, and spiritual encouragement.

CHAPTER VIII 
LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT AND OFFICER RESPONSIBILITIES 
 
 
8.1 Leadership Philosophy 
The Campus Christian Movement (CCM) believes that leadership is a sacred stewardship 
entrusted by God. Leadership is not a position of privilege or personal recognition but a 
calling to serve others with humility, integrity, wisdom, and love, following the example 
of Jesus Christ, who came "not to be served, but to serve" (Mark 10:45). 
 
Accordingly, CCM is committed to intentionally developing leaders who demonstrate 
spiritual maturity, Christ -like character, Biblical conviction, servant -heartedness, and a 
passion for making disciples. Leadership development is viewed as a lifelong process of 
spiritual formation, ministry experience, mentoring, and continuous learning. 
 
Every member is encouraged to grow as a disciple and discover opportunities to lead 
through faithful service. Leadership positions within CCM are entrusted to individuals 
who have demonstrated consistent Christian character, faithfulness in ministry, 
teachability, and readiness to assume greater responsibility. 
 
8.2 Objectives and Leadership Development 
The Leadership Development Program of CCM aims to: 
1. Develop Christ-centered leaders who exemplify Biblical character and servant 
leadership. 
2. Equip members with the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary for effective 
ministry. 
3. Foster spiritual maturity through intentional discipleship and mentoring. 
4. Prepare future officers and ministry leaders for increasing leadership 
responsibilities. 
5. Promote leadership continuity through systematic succession planning. 
6. Encourage every member to become a disciple -maker who faithfully advances 
the Great Commission. 
 
 
8.3 Leadership Development Pathway 
Leadership development follows the discipleship pathway established by the Campus 
Christian Movement. Members are encouraged to grow progressively through increasing 
levels of spiritual maturity, ministry involvement, and leadership responsibility (refer to 
Figure 6). 
 
Advancement along this pathway is based primarily on demonstrated Christian 
character, spiritual growth, faithfulness in ministry, teachability, and leadership 
readiness rather than length of membership alone.

CCM Manual of Operation 
37

Individuals entrusted with leadership responsibilities in CCM should strive to 
demonstrate the following qualifications:

• A growing personal relationship with Jesus Christ. 
• Commitment to regular prayer and the study of God's Word. 
• Consistent participation in discipleship and ministry activities. 
• A lifestyle that reflects Biblical values and Christian integrity. 
Character Qualifications 
• Humility and servant-heartedness. 
• Honesty and integrity. 
• Faithfulness and dependability. 
• Emotional maturity and self-control.

Student leaders shall also meet the eligibility requirements prescribed by the Constitution 
and By-Laws and the policies of J.H. Cerilles State College. 
 
8.5 Responsibilities of All Leaders  
Regardless of position, every officer and ministry leader shall: 
1. Model Christ-like character in both public and private life. 
2. Maintain a consistent devotional life through prayer and Scripture. 
3. Support the Vision, Mission, Core Values, and ministry objectives of CCM. 
4. Participate faithfully in meetings, ministry activities, and leadership 
development programs. 
5. Shepherd and encourage members under their care. 
6. Maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive matters. 
7. Demonstrate accountability in the use of organizational resources. 
8. Promote unity, reconciliation, and teamwork. 
9. Mentor potential future leaders.

• Coordinate regularly with the Executive Council.

8.8 Leadership Accountability 
Leadership within CCM is founded upon mutual accountability, servant leadership, and 
Biblical integrity. Officers and ministry leaders are expected to remain accountable to 
God, the Faculty Adviser, the Executive Council, fellow leaders, and the members th ey 
serve. 
 
Leaders shall welcome constructive feedback, participate in regular evaluation, and 
pursue continuous personal and spiritual growth. When concerns regarding leadership 
conduct or performance arise, they shall be addressed prayerfully, respectfully, and 
confidentially, with the primary goal of restoration, improvement, and faithfulness to the 
ministry. 
 
Persistent neglect of responsibilities, conduct inconsistent with the values of CCM, or 
violations of the Constitution and By -Laws, this Manual of Operations, or applicable 
College policies may result in appropriate corrective measures in accordance with 
established organizational procedures. 
 
8.9 Commissioning of Leaders 
The Campus Christian Movement recognizes the commissioning of leaders as both a 
privilege and a sacred responsibility. Newly appointed officers and ministry leaders shall 
be formally prayed over and commissioned before assuming their duties, signifying the  
organization's commitment to entrusting leadership under the guidance and 
empowerment of God. 
 
The commissioning ceremony shall emphasize servant leadership, faithful stewardship, 
and the shared responsibility of advancing the mission of making disciples. Leaders are 
encouraged to renew their commitment annually through prayer, reflection, and 
participation in leadership development activities.

faithful transfer of knowledge, ministry experience, and organizational resources. 
Through this process, CCM seeks to preserve its mission, values, and ministry culture 
while equipping each generation to lead with wisdom, humility, and Christ -like 
character.

CHAPTER IX 
ADMINISTRATIVE OPERATIONS 
 
9.1 General Administrative Policy 
The Campus Christian Movement (CCM) shall administer its affairs in a manner that 
reflects Biblical stewardship, servant leadership, accountability, transparency, and 
excellence. Administrative systems exist not merely to facilitate organizational efficiency 
but to support the faithful fulfillment of the organization's mission of making disciples. 
 
All administrative processes shall be conducted in accordance with the Constitution and 
By-Laws, this Manual of Operations, the policies of J.H. Cerilles  State College, and 
applicable laws and regulations. Officers and ministry leaders are expected to maintain 
integrity, confidentiality, accuracy, and professionalism in the performance of their 
administrative responsibilities. 
 
Planning, decision-making, communication, financial stewardship, documentation, and 
evaluation shall always support the spiritual mission of CCM and contribute to the 
effective operation of the organization. 
 
9.2 Ministry Planning 
Planning is an essential expression of faithful stewardship. CCM shall prepare ministry 
plans prayerfully and strategically to ensure that every activity advances the 
organization's Vision, Mission, Core Values, Campus to Community Framework, and the 
5R Ministry Cycle. 
 
Planning shall occur at three levels: 
 
Annual Planning 
At the beginning of each academic year, the Executive Council shall prepare the Annual 
Ministry Plan, which shall include: 
• Annual ministry theme 
• Strategic objectives 
• Calendar of activities 
• Budget projections 
• Leadership development plans 
• Evangelism and discipleship goals 
• Ministry evaluation schedule 
 
Semester Planning 
Before each semester, ministry leaders shall review the Annual Ministry Plan and prepare 
detailed implementation schedules, assigning responsibilities, timelines, and required 
resources.

CCM Manual of Operation 
42 
Activity Planning 
Every major activity shall have an Activity Proposal containing: 
• Objectives 
• Program design 
• Target participants 
• Budget 
• Logistics 
• Risk management considerations 
• Evaluation plan 
 
All major activities shall be approved by the Executive Council and endorsed by the 
Faculty Adviser before implementation. 
 
 
9.3 Meetings 
Regular meetings provide opportunities for prayer, planning, communication, 
accountability, and evaluation. 
 
The following meetings shall be conducted: 
 
Executive Council Meeting 
Held regularly to discuss organizational concerns, ministry plans, financial matters, 
reports, and upcoming activities. 
 
Leadership Meeting 
A gathering of officers, committee heads, ministry leaders, and Faith Circle Leaders for 
ministry coordination, leadership development, and strategic planning. 
 
Committee Meeting 
Conducted as needed by each committee for detailed planning and implementation. 
 
General Assembly 
Convened at least once each semester to communicate ministry directions, celebrate 
God's work, present organizational updates, and strengthen fellowship among members. 
Whenever practicable, meetings shall begin and end with prayer. Minutes shall be 
prepared for all official meetings and kept in the organization's permanent records. 
 
 
9.4 Decision-Making Process 
The Campus Christian Movement values prayerful, collaborative, and Biblically 
grounded decision -making. Leaders shall seek God's wisdom through prayer, 
consultation, and careful consideration before making significant organizational 
decisions.

CCM Manual of Operation 
43 
Whenever possible, decisions shall be reached through consensus, reflecting unity and 
mutual respect among leaders. When consensus cannot reasonably be achieved, matters 
may be decided by majority vote in accordance with the Constitution and By-Laws. 
 
Major decisions requiring Executive Council action include: 
• Approval of annual ministry plans 
• Approval of major events 
• Budget allocations 
• Creation or dissolution of committees 
• Organizational partnerships 
• Amendments to operational policies 
• Recommendations regarding leadership matters 
 
The Faculty Adviser shall be consulted on matters requiring institutional guidance or 
approval. 
 
 
9.5 Communication System 
Effective communication is essential to maintaining unity, coordination, and 
transparency within the organization. 
 
CCM shall utilize official communication channels, which may include: 
• Official Facebook Page 
• Official Facebook Group 
• Messenger Group Chats 
• Electronic mail (email) 
• Approved collaboration platforms 
• Official bulletin boards 
• Printed announcements 
 
Official announcements shall be released only through authorized officers or individuals 
designated by the Executive Council. 
 
Members are encouraged to communicate respectfully, responsibly, and truthfully. 
Digital communication shall reflect Christian integrity and uphold the reputation of both 
CCM and J.H. Cerilles State College. 
 
 
9.6 Records Management 
Accurate documentation preserves the institutional memory of the Campus Christian 
Movement and supports accountability, continuity, and effective ministry.

CCM Manual of Operation 
44 
The organization shall maintain the following records: 
• Constitution and By-Laws 
• Manual of Operations 
• Membership Database 
• Attendance Records 
• Minutes of Meetings 
• Financial Records 
• Annual Ministry Plans 
• Activity Proposals 
• Accomplishment Reports 
• Evaluation Reports 
• Leadership Records 
• Photo and Video Documentation 
• Official Correspondence 
 
Organizational records may be maintained in both printed and digital formats. Electronic 
records shall be backed up regularly and stored securely to prevent unauthorized access, 
loss, or damage. 
 
Confidential information shall be accessible only to authorized officers, the Faculty 
Adviser, or other persons duly authorized by the Executive Council. 
 
 
9.7 Reports and Evaluation 
Evaluation is an important component of faithful stewardship and continuous 
improvement. Ministry leaders shall regularly assess the effectiveness of programs, 
leadership, and organizational operations. 
 
The following reports shall be prepared as applicable: 
• Monthly Ministry Reports 
• Committee Reports 
• Financial Reports 
• Attendance Reports 
• Accomplishment Reports 
• Event Evaluation Reports 
• Annual Ministry Report 
Evaluation shall consider both measurable outcomes and spiritual impact, including 
participation, discipleship progress, leadership development, ministry effectiveness, and 
opportunities for improvement. 
 
Recommendations arising from evaluations shall inform future planning and 
organizational development.

CCM Manual of Operation

9.8 Calendar Management 
The Executive Council shall prepare and maintain the official CCM Ministry Calendar 
for each academic year. 
The calendar shall include: 
• Evangelism activities 
• Weekly gatherings 
• Leadership meetings 
• Discipleship programs 
• Prayer initiatives 
• Special events 
• Leadership trainings 
• Community outreach activities 
• Evaluation periods 
• College-recognized organizational requirements 
 
Any substantial revisions to the official calendar shall be communicated promptly to all 
concerned members and approved through the appropriate organizational processes. 
 
 
9.9 Continuous Improvement 
The Campus Christian Movement is committed to continuous learning and 
organizational improvement. Officers and ministry leaders shall regularly review 
ministry practices, administrative systems, leadership effectiveness, and organizational 
policies to ensure that the ministry remains faithful to its mission and responsive to the 
needs of students. 
 
Suggestions from members, alumni, partner churches, and the Faculty Adviser are 
welcomed and shall be prayerfully considered when appropriate. 
 
Operational improvements shall preserve the Biblical convictions, mission, and ministry 
philosophy of CCM while encouraging innovation, creativity, and excellence in serving 
God and the College community.

CHAPTER IX 
AMENDMENTS AND FINAL PROVISIONS 
 
 
10.1 Amendment of the Manual  
This Manual of Operations is intended to be a living document that provides guidance 
for the effective and orderly operation of the Campus Christian Movement (CCM). While 
its Biblical foundations, mission, and core values remain constant, its operational policies 
and procedures may be reviewed and revised to address the changing needs of the 
organization, provided that such amendments remain faithful to the Vision, Mission, 
Constitution and By-Laws, and the principles of Holy Scripture. 
 
Any proposed amendment to this Manual may originate from the Executive Council, the 
Faculty Adviser, a standing committee, or any member through a written 
recommendation submitted to the Executive Council for consideration. 
 
 
 
10.2 Amendment Procedure 
The following procedures shall govern amendments to this Manual: 
1. Proposed amendments shall be submitted in writing to the Executive Council, 
clearly indicating the sections to be amended and the reasons for the proposed 
revision. 
2. The Executive Council shall review the proposal and may consult committee 
heads, ministry leaders, or other members whose responsibilities may be affected 
by the proposed amendment. 
3. The Faculty Adviser shall review the proposed amendment to ensure its 
consistency with the Vision, Mission, Constitution and By -Laws of CCM, the 
policies of J.H. Cerilles State College, and applicable laws and regulations. 
4. Amendments shall be approved in accordance with the procedures prescribed 
by the Constitution and By -Laws or by a majority vote of the Executive Council 
when authorized to do so by the Constitution. 
5. Approved amendments shall immediately become part of this Manual and shall 
be incorporated into future editions. 
6. The Secretary shall maintain an official record of all approved amendments, 
including the date of approval, the nature of the amendment, and the approving 
authority. 
 
 
10.3 Interpretation 
Questions regarding the interpretation or application of any provision of this Manual 
shall be referred to the Executive Council for initial clarification. When necessary, the 
Faculty Adviser shall provide guidance, particularly on matters involving instit utional 
policies or issues not expressly addressed by this Manual.

CCM Manual of Operation

In the event of any conflict between this Manual and the Constitution and By-Laws of the 
Campus Christian Movement, the provisions of the Constitution and By -Laws shall 
prevail. Likewise, all organizational operations shall remain subject to the policies a nd 
regulations of J.H. Cerilles State College. 
 
 
10.4 Separability Clause 
Should any provision of this Manual be declared invalid, unenforceable, or inconsistent 
with applicable laws or institutional policies, such declaration shall not affect the validity 
of the remaining provisions, which shall continue to remain in full force and effect. 
 
 
10.5 Repealing Cause 
All previous operational guidelines, administrative practices, memoranda, or policies of 
the Campus Christian Movement that are inconsistent with the provisions of this Manual 
are hereby repealed, amended, or modified accordingly. 
 
Existing practices that are not inconsistent with this Manual may continue to be observed 
until superseded by duly approved policies or procedures. 
 
 
10.6 Effectivity 
This Manual of Operations shall take effect immediately upon its approval by the 
Executive Council, endorsement by the Faculty Adviser, and recognition by the 
appropriate office of J.H. Cerilles State College, where required. 
 
All officers, ministry leaders, committee heads, members, and volunteers of the Campus 
Christian Movement shall be guided by and faithfully observe the provisions of this 
Manual in carrying out the mission and ministries of the organization. 
 
10.7 Statement of Commitment 
The Campus Christian Movement affirms that this Manual of Operations is more than a collection 
of administrative policies. It is a shared commitment to honor God through orderly, faithful, and 
Christ-centered ministry. 
 
As officers, leaders, advisers, and members, we dedicate ourselves to faithfully uphold the Vision, 
Mission, Core Values, Constitution and By-Laws, and the provisions of this Manual. We commit 
to serve with humility, integrity, excellence, and love, recogn izing that every ministry entrusted 
to us is ultimately for the glory of God and the advancement of His Kingdom. 
 
May every program, decision, relationship, and act of service undertaken through the Campus 
Christian Movement contribute to fulfilling the Great Commission of our Lord Jesus Christ,

faith, cultivate Christian fellowship, and actively participate in God's mission of making 
disciples.
